title: lore new does not scaffold a profile type's declared sections, so its own output fails lore validate immediately
description:
Reported by opum-agent 2026-09-18, measured against the installed 0.7.0 binary. Independently
re-verified here against dev at HEAD, via `bun run src/cli.ts` in a throwaway bundle -- STILL
PRESENT, not already fixed.

THE DEFECT: a profile type's declared `sections` are ENFORCED by `lore validate` but not
SCAFFOLDED by `lore new`, so the tool's own scaffold generates a file the tool's own validator
immediately rejects.

Minimal repro, confirmed here:

  # .lore/profile.toml
  [[types]]
  name = "Feature"
  sections = ["Problem", "Behaviour", "Acceptance criteria"]

  lore new feature "Probe feature"    # body: "Describe this Feature here."
  lore validate                        # exit 6, three [required-section] errors

Confirmed exit 6 with exactly three `required-section` errors naming the three declared headings,
none of which the generated body contains.

ROOT CAUSE, located: src/core/template.ts:328-329, `builtinTemplateFor`:

  export function builtinTemplateFor(type: string): string {
    return Object.hasOwn(BUILTIN_TEMPLATES, type) ? (BUILTIN_TEMPLATES[type] as string) : GENERIC_TEMPLATE;
  }

`BUILTIN_TEMPLATES` (template.ts:451-459) is a fixed map keyed by lore's OWN seven built-in type
names, deliberately independent of the active profile (the file's own comment: "a custom-profile
type lore ships no body for falls back to GENERIC_TEMPLATE, and the project supplies its own
template file"). `GENERIC_TEMPLATE` (template.ts:466-470) is just `# {{title}}` + "Describe this
{{type}} here." -- no awareness of `profile.types.get(type)?.sections` at all, even though that
exact list is available (it is what `lore validate` reads to build the required-section errors,
via `requiredSectionsFor` in src/core/schema.ts:252-254).

THE TENSION WORTH RECORDING: template.ts's own module header states `lore new`'s output "validates
**by construction**" (ADR-0006 SS6; LORE-18 AC#1) -- but that guarantee has a carved-out exception,
stated in the BUILTIN_TEMPLATES comment, for exactly this case: a custom-profile type with no
matching template file. The guarantee and the documented exception coexist in the same file without
either cross-referencing the other, so a reader of the header alone would not learn the exception
exists until they hit it. Whether that carve-out should stay a carve-out, or whether `lore new`
should derive a heading skeleton from `sections` the same way it derives everything else about a
profile-declared type, is the actual design decision this task exists to make -- not prescribed here.

WHY IT MATTERS IN PRACTICE: out of the box, declaring a custom type with required sections means
`lore new` for that type is *guaranteed* to fail `lore validate` on the very first run, with no
warning at `new` time. The author has to already know to hand-write a template before ever running
`lore new` successfully for their own type -- exactly backwards from the zero-config built-in
experience the rest of the tool provides.

FIX SHAPE, not prescribed, two candidates recorded so the record captures the tradeoff rather than
just the symptom:
 1. Auto-derive a heading skeleton from `profile.types.get(type)?.sections` when no template file
    exists (closes the gap, but "the project supplies its own template file" then only applies to
    field-level content, not section shape).
 2. Keep the current fallback, but have `lore new` warn immediately (not just at the next `validate`)
    when it is about to scaffold a file it knows will fail its own gate, since the section list is
    already in hand at `new` time.
Whoever takes this should pick one and say why, per this repo's own convention for a design-shape
decision rather than a mechanical fix.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is recorded and argued: either lore new auto-derives a heading skeleton from a profile types declared sections when no template file exists, or lore new warns at scaffold time (not only at the next lore validate) that the generated file will fail validation -- not both silently attempted, one chosen with reasoning.

Whichever shape is chosen, the minimal repro in this task (a Feature type with three declared sections, no template file) produces a lore new result that either validates cleanly or is accompanied by an explicit, immediate warning naming the missing sections.

template.ts module header (the validates-by-construction claim, ADR-0006 SS6 / LORE-18 AC#1) is reconciled with whatever the chosen behavior is, so the header and the BUILTIN_TEMPLATES fallback comment stop describing two different guarantees in the same file.
bun run lint, typecheck and the test suite pass, and lore check exits 0.

implementationNotes:
Dedupe check, 2026-09-18: opum-agent's follow-up relay (item #2 of four) asked for "make
'validates by construction' true, or drop the claim" against template.ts's ADR-0006 SS6 header --
that is this task verbatim, not a separate ask. No new task filed for it; this record already
scopes the decision (auto-derive vs warn-at-scaffold-time) and the header reconciliation. Filed
LCLI-537/538 instead for the other two items in that relay that are genuinely new.
finalSummary: Fixed and delivered in PR #176. AC#1 DECISION, ARGUED AND CHOSEN: lore new AUTO-DERIVES a heading skeleton from a profile type's declared sections when no template file exists. The alternative -- warn at scaffold time that the generated file will fail validation -- was rejected for three reasons. (a) It leaves the user holding a file the tool KNOWS is wrong, when the tool also knows exactly which headings are missing and can simply write them; a warning spends the user's attention to avoid work the tool could do. (b) It duplicates a diagnostic that already exists: lore validate already names each missing section, so warn-at-scaffold would emit a second message for the same condition at a different moment. (c) Auto-derive is CONSISTENT with existing behaviour rather than a new convention -- BUILTIN_TEMPLATES already ship exactly this skeleton for every built-in type, so the change makes profile-declared types behave like built-in ones instead of inventing a third rule. The cost accepted: lore new writes empty headings a user may not want. That cost is already paid for every built-in type today and nobody has objected to it. DEFECT AND FIX: a profile type's declared sections are ENFORCED by lore validate but were not SCAFFOLDED by lore new, because a profile-declared type falls through to the lenient GENERIC_TEMPLATE which carries no sections. Built-in types were unaffected only because their hand-written templates already carry theirs -- which is why the new branch is keyed off hasBuiltinTemplate rather than applied unconditionally, leaving the built-in skeletons untouched. template.ts stays decoupled from the profile as its own comment requires: sectionScaffoldTemplate takes plain strings and is a pure formatter; the profile lookup lives in new.ts. Headings emit at ## because that is the only depth requiredSectionFindings matches. AC#2 VERIFIED with this task's own minimal repro: a Feature type declaring Problem/Behaviour/Acceptance criteria and no template file now scaffolds all three and lore validate reports 0 errors, 0 warnings. AC#3 DONE: the module header's validates-by-construction claim is reconciled with the BUILTIN_TEMPLATES note -- it now enumerates the three body sources and states which lore guarantees, naming the user-template override as deliberately outside the claim. MUTATION-TESTED with the red set predicted from the test file beforehand: removing the branch reddens the two scaffolding tests and leaves the no-sections test green; making the branch unconditional reddens exactly the no-sections test. One of the three tests asserts through the VALIDATOR rather than by string match, so a fix emitting the right text at the wrong heading depth would still be caught. AC#4 EVIDENCE: CI run 35406471266 on head a178e186 -- all five contexts required by dev's ruleset concluded PASS with zero non-pass jobs anywhere, including the lore check docs gate. Full suite 3288 pass / 0 fail; typecheck and lint exit 0. NOTE: that run predates this final header-reconciliation commit, which is comment-only; the re-run on the new head is the one to cite for the merged state.
